choiceTexts: One ketone and one carboxylic acid

answer.line: Each alkene carbon carries two carbon groups and no H. Cut the C=C, put an O on each carbon, and both become ketones.

steps: Look at the two alkene carbons. Each holds a methyl and a ring carbon, and neither holds an H.
Cut the C=C and put =O on each of its carbons. The ring opens into one chain.
A carbon with two carbon groups becomes a ketone. Both qualify, so the product is heptane-2,6-dione, a diketone.

choices.note: Plain cyclopentene has an H on each alkene carbon, so it gives a dialdehyde. Here the methyls take those spots.
Acids come from alkene carbons with an H, under an oxidative workup such as H2O2. Zn and acetic acid is reductive, and these carbons have no H anyway.

choices.text: One ketone and one carboxylic acid
choices.note: That is 1-methylcyclopentene with an oxidative workup. This alkene has two methyls, and the workup is reductive.
With one methyl, one alkene carbon keeps an H and becomes an aldehyde. Here both carbons carry a methyl.
Two carbon groups on each alkene carbon, so two ketones.

lockIt: Ozonolysis with a reductive workup: an alkene carbon with an H becomes an aldehyde, one without becomes a ketone.
